newsitem.title: UK: MP's death cuts Major's parliament majority to one.
newsitem.headline: MP's death cuts Major's parliament majority to one.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major's majority in parliament was cut to just one seat on Sunday when it was announced that one of his Conservative members of parliament, Barry Porter, had died.

The death raised the prospect of Major heading a minority government if the Conservatives lose Porter's Wirrall South constituency at a by-election and the opposition Labour Party retain a seat in another constituency in Northern England.
Porter died after a brief illness, a spokeswoman at Conservative headquarters said. Major issued a statement saying his death was "a shock and a sadness to his many friends".

Porter, who had held his seat since 1983, won a majority of 8,183 votes over Labour at the 1992 general election. But far bigger majorities have been surrendered by the Conservatives during the course of the present parliament.

With his party lagging Labour by more than 20 points in most recent opinion polls, Major is believed to want to delay the next general election until May next year, the last month on which it can constitutionally be held.

Even if he loses his overall parliamentary majority, he may be able to do so by relying on the support of small parties such as the nine-strong Official Ulster Unionists, whose main policy plank is that Northern Ireland must remain British.
